findings.summary: The journey now runs b3 (operation.connection.revoke) before the confirm/cancel branch b6, so revocation happens before the owner confirms; this contradicts the new rule that nothing is revoked until confirmation.
findings.evidence: b2 next: to b3; b3 operation: operation.connection.revoke, next: to b6; b6 'Confirm block or cancel in BlockConfirmDialog' vs ontology effect 'Nothing is revoked or recorded until the owner confirms in BlockConfirmDialog'

findings.summary: The cancel path (b6 -> e2) comes after revocation has already run in b3, so cancelling cannot leave sharing and pending jobs untouched as the updated criterion requires.
findings.evidence: criteria: 'Cancelling a block confirmation leaves sharing and pending jobs untouched'; journey: b3 revoke -> b6 { to: e2, when: cancel }
